feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications leader: the experience shows clear progression, relevant scope, and solid public-sector specialization. It is well written overall, but it feels slightly dense and repetitive, with some structure choices that dilute impact and a few style/consistency issues.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression within NACo, culminating in director-level leadership and now consulting; this strengthens credibility and narrative.  
- Good use of scale and specificity in key achievements (10,000+ pages, 3.5 million annual page views, 50+ publishers, named tools/platforms).  
- Strong positioning for digital platform, governance, analytics, and multimedia leadership in mission-driven organizations.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication across “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT”; consolidate to create a tighter, more scannable structure. The “Recent Projects” content in the footer should be moved into a dedicated section.  
- Add more outcome-focused results beyond activity descriptions: e.g., engagement growth, efficiency gains, adoption improvements, campaign performance, or cost savings.  
- Fix style consistency issues: “Coleman DAVIS” capitalization is unusual; punctuation in lists is inconsistent (e.g., “social, and multimedia” has an unnecessary comma); “A2/Learning” reads awkwardly—use “A2 (learning).” No major misspellings or grammar errors otherwise.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro with clear seniority and sector focus. It reads well, but it’s slightly dense and repeats themes already covered in the subtitle, competencies, and work experience.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten the first sentence and make the value proposition more direct: “Senior digital leader with 12+ years leading public-sector web platforms, governance, and content operations at scale.”
- Replace “building the platforms” with stronger leadership language such as “leading modernization of” or “overseeing.”
- Consider adding one concrete scale signal from recent roles, e.g., “10,000+ page website” or “3.5M annual page views,” to increase impact.
- Streamline the second sentence by grouping related areas: “Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics, editorial workflows, multimedia, and AI-enabled search/content experiences for mission-driven organizations.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled user experiences” overlaps with Core Competencies and Recent Projects; “AI-enabled search/content experiences” would align better with the CV.
- “Platforms, governance models and content operations” is close to the subtitle and competencies; simplify to avoid repetition.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and work experience. Tightening the phrasing and emphasizing higher-level leadership capabilities will make it feel less repetitive and more executive.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel noun phrases and shorten longer items for cleaner scanning.
- Replace “operations” repetition with more distinct capability language.
- Prioritize the most senior, differentiating strengths first: modernization, governance, analytics, AI/search.
- Suggested rewrite: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial systems • Analytics, reporting, and insight infrastructure • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integration • Multi-channel communications leadership • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia production and livestreaming

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise website modernization,” “AI-enabled search,” “analytics infrastructure,” and “multimedia production” are already prominent in the header and Topline Skills.
- “Advocacy and public-sector communications” overlaps with both the header and Topline Skills; consider keeping either “public-sector” or “advocacy,” not both.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it largely repeats achievements already covered in Work Experience. Tightening phrasing and adding clearer outcomes or scope would make it feel more distinct and impactful.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add dates or “Selected Recent Projects” framing to reinforce recency and separate this from core experience.
- Use parallel, tighter phrasing: “Led/Built/Developed” + platform/scope + outcome.
- Replace generic terms like “improve discovery” and “continued campaign growth” with specific results, audience, or organizational value where possible.
- Standardize style and punctuation; spell out “10-by-20-foot” for consistency.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite work, and advocacy video series closely overlap with current NACo bullets; this footer should emphasize standout examples, outcomes, or formats not already stated.
- The anniversary campaign is the most distinct item here; consider leading with it to reduce repetition.

items.title: Coleman DAVIS
items.subtitle: Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader
items.content: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Email
items.content: coleman@colemanpdavis.com

items.title: Website
items.content: https://colemanpdavis.com/

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant current role, but it reads like a broad service list and overlaps heavily with your 2022–2024 NACo leadership entry. Make it tighter, more senior, and focused on what is new since returning as a consultant.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + value: “Advise NACo on enterprise digital strategy, Drupal platform enhancements, and cross-channel content operations for member-facing communications.”
- Combine overlapping duties into 3–4 impact-led bullets; e.g., “Designed and implemented Drupal microsite and modular content frameworks to accelerate campaign launches and improve toolkit publishing.”
- Rephrase technical work to show outcomes: “Streamlined digital workflows, analytics, and governance to improve coordination across web, email, social, and multimedia teams.”
- Keep the AI work as the differentiator and add metrics if possible: “Led AI-enabled search initiative, defining retrieval strategy, structured content model, and discovery UX to improve findability of member resources.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Governance, workflows, analytics, and enterprise web improvement” repeats themes already covered in Director of Digital Media.
- “CMS development/front-end implementation” may duplicate skills sections unless tied to a concrete result.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with solid scale indicators. It should be tightened to emphasize executive ownership and outcomes, while avoiding overlap with the adjacent NACo roles on newsletters, video, and workflow coordination.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper scope/outcome line: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Combine and tighten channel bullets; prioritize scale and transformation: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Add measurable results where possible for email/social/video/analytics (growth, engagement, cost savings, production volume, reporting speed, adoption).
- Rephrase operational bullets to show business impact: “Established governance, publishing standards, and cross-department planning systems that improved consistency, accountability, and decision-making.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Email newsletters reaching tens of thousands” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep that detail there unless you can add higher-level outcomes here.
- “Built first in-house video studio” may partially overlap with earlier video-production bullets; frame this here as capacity-building and operational scale.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more clearly about execution, channel growth, and editorial operations at the manager-to-director transition level.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + function: “Directed day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social, and video, supporting NACo’s advocacy messaging and cross-channel editorial execution.”
- Tighten bullets around distinct contributions: managed four weekly newsletters; produced and scaled a weekly advocacy video update; coordinated editorial planning across communications, advocacy, and program teams.
- Replace soft phrasing like “helped improve” with stronger ownership: “standardized digital publishing workflows to improve consistency, coordination, and turnaround time.”
- Add metrics if available: newsletter open/click rates, subscriber growth, video cadence/views, publishing volume, or reduction in production time.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “video as a recurring channel” overlaps with the 2015–2018 role; keep this focused on scaling/formalizing, not launching.
- “editorial coordination/workflows” overlaps with the 2022–2024 role; avoid governance language better reserved for the Director entry.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this topline item overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent NACo roles. Tighten it to emphasize senior-level scope and distinct value rather than repeating generic communications language.

Suggested edit
- Recast as sharper, higher-signal phrases tied to recent leadership scope:
- Enterprise digital strategy & platform modernization
- Editorial governance, publishing workflows & content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership (web, email, social, video)
- Public-sector, membership & advocacy messaging
- Audience-centered content strategy & information architecture
- Replace “audience-focused content planning” with “audience-centered content strategy & information architecture” to sound more senior and differentiated.
- Consider adding one concrete scale marker if format allows, e.g., “10,000+ page ecosystems” or “50+ publishers,” drawn from the Director role.
- Keep wording parallel and noun-based; avoid mixing broad leadership terms with lower-level task phrasing.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Multi-channel communications leadership” duplicates Core Competencies’ “Multi-channel communication.”
- “Editorial systems and governance” overlaps with “Editorial workflow design” and recent NACo bullets on governance/publishing standards.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads as a raw tool list and overlaps heavily with the separate “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize higher-value capabilities and recent, proven strengths from NACo rather than repeating every platform.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as capability-led, not software-led: “Drupal platform leadership • CMS modernization & migration • Front-end implementation (HTML/CSS/JavaScript) • API integrations & workflow automation • Airtable-based systems • AI-enabled search and content discovery”
- Prioritize recent strengths tied to experience: keep Drupal, CMS modernization, AI-enabled search, and workflow automation; de-emphasize older/lower-signal items like jQuery unless required by target roles.
- Tighten phrasing: change “AI-enabled search experiences” to “AI-enabled search and content discovery” and “Airtable systems” to “Airtable-based systems.”
- If possible, align with evidence from experience by implying scale: e.g., “Enterprise Drupal platforms” or “Large-scale CMS modernization.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates much of “Technical + IT”; avoid repeating WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages, HTML/CSS/JavaScript, and API integrations in both places.
- “CMS modernization” already echoes Core Competencies and work history; keep it here only if phrased more specifically.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tool stack for the recent director/consulting work, but the line reads as a generic keyword list. It would be stronger if grouped around business value and trimmed to avoid overlap with “Data analytics & reporting” in Core Competencies.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-only to capability + outcome language, e.g. “Analytics strategy, reporting & optimization.”
- Group items for clarity: “GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Looker Studio, Power BI, BigQuery” + “KPI framework design, executive reporting, SEO/performance analysis.”
- Consider a tighter rewrite: “GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Looker Studio, Power BI & BigQuery • KPI framework design • Executive/leadership reporting • SEO and digital performance optimization”
- If you can support it elsewhere, align with impact from recent roles: dashboards for 3.5M annual page views, cross-channel reporting, or decision support for 50+ publishers.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Leadership reporting” may read weaker than “executive reporting” and overlaps with “Data analytics & reporting” in Core Competencies.
- Avoid repeating the exact same analytics tool list in role bullets unless tied to a measurable result.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong supporting skill area, but it reads generic and overlaps with both Core Competencies and multiple NACo experience bullets. Make it more senior, specific, and aligned to recent in-house studio/event leadership.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to emphasize scope: “Multimedia Production, Studio & Live Event Delivery.”
- Tighten and elevate phrasing: “Broadcast-quality video production and editing • Livestream and webcast production • PTZ camera and multi-camera studio systems • Studio buildout and operations • Hybrid and virtual event delivery”
- If space allows, add one higher-value capability instead of a basic one: replace “Livestreaming” with “Live broadcast workflows” or “End-to-end event production.”
- Consider reflecting leadership/ownership rather than task execution, since recent roles show you built and led capability.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This partially duplicates “Multimedia & live event production” in Core Competencies; keep this version more technical/tactical.
- “Hybrid and virtual event production” overlaps with NACo studio/event bullets, so avoid repeating the same wording elsewhere.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it reads as a duplicate of “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills and misses a chance to signal depth. Since recent experience is heavily Drupal-centered, lead with that and add level/context rather than just names.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by relevance/recency: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- Add proficiency framing, e.g. **Drupal (enterprise CMS, migration, modular content architecture)** if your format allows short qualifiers.
- If keeping as a pure skills line, tighten to the platforms you’ve used meaningfully in recent roles; consider dropping **GitHub Pages** if it’s not central to target roles.
- Alternative rewrite: **Drupal (enterprise web, migrations, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially overlaps with **Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; consider merging or making this one platform-only and the other execution-focused.
- “Web & CMS administration” already appears in Core Competencies, so avoid repeating generic CMS wording here.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but this item reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Make it more current, implementation-focused, and slightly more senior to match recent Drupal/CMS modernization work.

Suggested edit
- Rename to: Front-End & Technical Implementation
- Tighten and modernize phrasing: HTML/CSS • JavaScript/jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
- If accurate, add level/context instead of just tools: Front-end implementation for Drupal and CMS environments • API integrations • tag management • edge/serverless scripting • deployment automation
- If space allows, replace older terms with evidence of use: Built front-end components, managed GTM deployments, created Cloudflare Workers scripts, and automated workflows via GitHub Actions

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the exact same wording in both places.
- GTM may also fit under Analytics/Optimization if that section needs stronger technical depth.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful tools, but this item is currently just a software list and overlaps with stronger “workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” positioning elsewhere. It should emphasize systems you actively build or manage, not generic collaboration apps.

Suggested edit:
- Narrow to tools that signal workflow design/automation depth: “Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana”
- Move general collaboration tools out or drop them: Slack, Teams, Basecamp, and Trello read as everyday workplace platforms, not differentiating technical skills.
- Consider retitling to sharpen relevance: “Workflow Automation & Project Systems”
- If space allows, add light functional framing instead of a pure list: “Airtable (operational databases) • Power Automate, Zapier (workflow automation) • Jira, Asana (project/workflow management)”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same language verbatim.
- Jira/Asana overlap with broader coordination themes in Core Competencies, so keep this item tool-specific.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant platforms, but this line is too bare compared with the rest of the CV and misses the scale/ownership implied by recent email leadership work. Make it more specific and aligned to systems administration, campaign execution, or audience engagement.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms**
- If accurate, expand to: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp • Email campaign operations • Newsletter publishing • Audience segmentation**
- If you directly administered these tools, use: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp • Template management • List segmentation • Journey/campaign setup**
- Keep only platforms/features you used recently and substantively; lead with the system most relevant to current target roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item overlaps with repeated “email/newsletters” references in Work Experience; avoid adding generic phrases like “email marketing” unless paired with concrete system functions.
- “Engagement” may duplicate broader multi-channel claims elsewhere unless tied specifically to membership/community platforms like Higher Logic.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list, but it overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills” and misses a chance to show level of capability. Tighten it into a sharper technical stack line and emphasize analysis/optimization methods rather than repeating platform names elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: **GA4 • BigQuery • Power BI • Looker Studio • Microsoft Clarity • SEO analysis • A/B testing • KPI dashboarding**
- Replace vague **“SEO”** with **“SEO analysis”** or **“search performance analysis”** to sound more execution-focused.
- Replace **“Dashboarding”** with **“KPI dashboarding”** or **“executive reporting dashboards”** for clearer business value.
- If space allows elsewhere, tie these tools to outcomes in recent roles instead of adding more tools here (e.g., analytics infrastructure supporting 3.5M annual page views).

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates **Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization**; consider keeping the fuller version in one place only.
- GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery are already named in the 2022–2024 role, so avoid expanding this list further.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal and useful “first in-house digital team” context, but the item is still broad and overlaps with the stronger 2018–2024 NACo entries. Make it more execution-focused and concrete, with 1–2 specific outputs or scale indicators.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe around early-career buildout and delivery: “Promoted across two digital roles to help establish NACo’s first in-house digital team…”
- Tighten phrasing and reduce generic terms like “high-impact” and “strengthening workflows”; replace with specific actions and channels.
- Add measurable scope if available: number of livestreams/videos produced, size of web refresh, email/social volume, or team support.
- Possible rewrite: “Promoted across two digital roles to help establish NACo’s first in-house digital team. Supported web, email, social and multimedia operations; contributed to a major website refresh; produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates; and provided day-to-day direction to a digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; differentiate this item as launch/build phase.
- Avoid repeating workflow/governance language already covered more strongly in later NACo roles.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This is a useful early-career entry, but it reads generically and overlaps with later NACo roles in digital/multimedia. Emphasize the podcast launch and frame the rest as support to policy/program initiatives.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground the clearest achievement: “Supported innovation and policy research initiatives for county-facing programs, while expanding NACo’s early digital content efforts.”
- Add a stronger second sentence: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading episode planning, scripting, coordination, and production.”
- Replace vague phrases like “contributed to digital content production” with specific outputs if possible: multimedia assets, web stories, interviews, or stakeholder-facing materials.
- If you have metrics, add one: number of episodes launched, audience/downloads, projects supported, or teams/stakeholders coordinated.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid overemphasizing broad digital/media leadership here; that is covered much more strongly in 2015–2024 roles.
- “Multimedia production” repeats later entries, so keep this item focused on podcast launch + innovation/research support.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too generic and overlaps heavily with “Multimedia Production & Event Delivery” and multiple work bullets. In a senior CV, this section should emphasize tools only, with production capabilities framed more precisely or moved elsewhere.

Suggested edit
